get.description:
The last enrichment LoneScale holds for a contact, so you can keep your own long-lived cache and skip an enrichment you have already paid for.

**This is a per-contact record, not a log of your calls.** Three limits follow from that, worth reading before you build on it:

- At most **one entry per contact**: the latest state we know, not one entry per `/trigger/enrich` call. `providers` and `credits` are therefore not returned, since they are not retained per contact.
- An enrichment that **found nothing leaves no entry**. A contact we searched and missed is indistinguishable from one we never searched: both return an empty `data`.
- A hit on the 24h enrichment cache does **not** refresh `date`. It is the date of the last enrichment that actually ran, which is the date your cache should key on.

The history is scoped to your API key: you only ever read contacts your own account enriched.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description:
The contact, as an email, a phone number, a LinkedIn profile URL or a CRM record id. URL-encode the value (`+` in a phone number especially). A LinkedIn URL can also be passed as its bare vanity slug (`jane-doe`), which avoids encoding slashes altogether.

Emails and phone numbers match secondary values too, not just the main one, and a phone number matches whatever spelling we stored it in: `+33621114568` and `+33 6 21 11 45 68` find the same contact.

One case to know about: a contact that only ever reached LoneScale through this API, never through a CRM sync or a list import, carries no CRM id and, if you asked for `email` or `phone` alone, no LinkedIn URL either. Look those up by the email or phone we returned.

parameters.name: include_data
parameters.description: Return the enriched contact itself in `data`. Off by default: the entry otherwise carries only what happened, not the data.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Entries come back newest first.

200.description: The contact's enrichment history. Empty `data` when the contact was never enriched on your account, or was searched without a result.

Search contacts synchronously and return results directly in the response — no webhook required.

The response contains all sourced contacts in a single call. **Maximum 10 contacts per request.** Rate limited to **5 requests per minute**.

**Time budget.** A sync call answers within about 45 seconds. Personas are searched in the order you send them and share the `limit`, so put the most important ones first. When the budget runs out before the limit is reached, the response has `partial: true`: retry with fewer personas, or use the asynchronous endpoint `/trigger/contact-sourcing` with a `webhook_url`, which has no time budget. Only the contacts returned are charged.

get.description:
Resolve a single company by domain, LinkedIn id, LinkedIn slug, or name and return a stable, fixed-shape result.

At least one of `domain`, `linkedin_id`, `slug`, or `name` is required. The response always returns the same set of fields — `null` (or `[]` for arrays) is used for any field we do not have data for, so client integrations can rely on a stable schema.

When `enrich=true` and no cached match is found, the API will trigger an on-demand enrichment via data-sync; when `enrich=true` and a result has both a LinkedIn id and a universal name, a function-by-function headcount breakdown is also attached.

The optional `custom` map (e.g. `custom[crm_id]=abc-123`) is echoed back unchanged at the top level of the response — useful for correlating results with records on your side.

Rate limited to **5 requests per minute**.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Company domain (e.g. `stripe.com`). Schemes, `www.`, paths, and casing are normalized server-side.

parameters.name: linkedin_id
parameters.description: Numeric LinkedIn company id (the digits in `linkedin.com/company/{id}`).

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: LinkedIn universal name / slug (the trailing segment in `linkedin.com/company/{slug}`).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Company name. Best-effort match — prefer `domain`, `linkedin_id`, or `slug` for deterministic resolution.

parameters.name: enrich
parameters.description: When `true`, fall back to on-demand enrichment if no cached match is found, and attach a `headcount` breakdown when possible. Defaults to `false`.

parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Arbitrary key/value passthrough echoed unchanged in the response — useful for correlating results with records on your side. Pass a **URL-encoded JSON object**, e.g. `custom=%7B%22crm_id%22%3A%22abc-123%22%2C%22priority%22%3A1%7D` (decodes to `{"crm_id":"abc-123","priority":1}`). Only flat string/number values are kept — nested objects, arrays, booleans and null are dropped.

200.description: Search completed. `results` contains at most one company, or is empty when nothing matched.

400.description: Invalid input — typically no filter provided, or an empty filter value.

example.message: at least one of name, domain, linkedin_id, slug is required

429.description: Rate limit exceeded — max 5 requests per minute

post.description:
Push contacts and/or companies directly into your connected CRM. LoneScale creates or updates the records asynchronously, applying the team-level integration field mappings already configured in LoneScale (create/update fields and unicity criteria). No workflow is involved.

Record keys must match the LoneScale field keys referenced by your configured mappings (for example `lonescale_first_name`, `lonescale_company_domain`, or any custom key you mapped); see [Available Fields](/api-reference/crm-sync-fields) for the full list. For Salesforce the mapping also decides the object: map only the Lead section and the sync searches, updates or creates Leads instead of Contacts. Set `account_crm_id` on a record to target an existing CRM company by id instead of matching by unicity criteria.

Poll `GET /trigger/crm-sync/{id}` with the returned `id`, or pass a `webhook_url` to be called once with the run summary when every record has been processed.

post.description: Look up contacts and companies in your connected CRM(s) and surface the record owner. Two forms. **Flat**: one contact, with `email`, `linkedin_url`, or a name with a company; the answer is `matches`. **Records**: `contacts` and/or `companies`, the same free-form records as `POST /trigger/crm-sync` (`lonescale_*` keys, bare `company_*` and camelCase aliases, `account_crm_id`), at most 20 in all; each record is searched on its own and answered under its index in `contacts[i]` / `companies[i]`, so you can pre-check the exact payload you are about to sync. Companies are matched, in order, by CRM id, by your company unicity criteria (of the `settings_type` record), by LinkedIn page, by domain, by exact name (`matchedOn` says which). Only connected CRMs are queried. Pipedrive and Sellsy search contacts by email and companies by name only. Each match carries `owned_by_you`, and `caller_crm_links` tells which CRM user the caller is linked to, so a client can say "already yours" vs "owned by X" and warn when a create would go to the default owner.

The accounts of a CRM book worth working today, best first (10 at most). An account gets in with a LoneScale signal in the last 30 days on its domain (job change, new hire, contact sourced, hiring burst; job postings over 14 days) and no CRM activity in the last 7 days. Each account comes with the signal, the person to reach (with the email and phone already known), its owner, the last touch and a score with the lines it adds up from (`score_parts`).

This returns the last list computed for the book. `status: none` means it was never ranked: call `POST /todays-accounts/refresh`, then poll this endpoint while `status` is `pending`.

Requires Today's accounts to be enabled for the API key's holder. Rate limited to **30 requests per minute**.

post.description:
Skips one of the listed accounts for the whole organization. The CRM is not touched. `reason` says what happens next: `BAD_TIMING` (default) and `OTHER` hide it until a newer signal arrives on it; `IN_PROGRESS` hides it for 90 days whatever comes; `NOT_ICP` hides it and, once two accounts of the same industry were dismissed this way, takes 2 points off that industry's accounts in the ranking; `WRONG_CONTACT` keeps the account, never proposes that person on it again and swaps in the next contact.

Rate limited to **30 requests per minute**.

When `true`, the webhook response will include a `jobChangeDetected` field indicating whether the contact has changed company since the input data was provided.

Only effective when `enrichment_type` includes `"profile"` and `webhook_url` is provided.

force_refresh.description: Opt out of the 24h enrichment cache for this call. When a contact was already enriched for your account within the last 24 hours, the cached result is returned and no credits are consumed; pass `true` to force a fresh enrichment instead (credits are consumed and the cache entry is refreshed).

sync_to_crm.description:
Push the enriched contact into your connected CRM. Disabled by default: without it, this endpoint only enriches and never writes to your CRM.

When `true`, the write-back uses the integration mapping configured for the **Chrome extension** (contact unicity criteria, create fields, company create fields). It can therefore **create** contacts and companies that did not exist, and the created records are owned by the CRM user linked to the API key holder.

To push records to your CRM with a dedicated mapping and a run status, use `POST /trigger/crm-sync` instead.

source.description: Reserved for LoneScale-hosted callers (the Slack bot). Meters the enrichment on the API key holder's per-user Chrome quota instead of the organization balance, and answers 403 when that quota is reached. Requires `source_signature`; leave both unset for integrations.

To push records to your CRM with a dedicated mapping and a run status, use `POST /trigger/crm-sync` instead.

Only present in the webhook payload when `detect_job_change: true` was set in the request. Detection first compares company domains using fuzzy matching, falling back to company name if domains are unavailable.

linkedinTagline.example: Help increase the GDP of the internet.

headcount.description: Function-by-function employee breakdown. Only populated when `enrich=true` AND the result has both `linkedinId` and `linkedinUniversalName`.

CrmSyncRecord.description: Free-form record: keys must match the LoneScale field keys referenced by the configured mappings. See [Available Fields](/api-reference/crm-sync-fields) for the full list. The `lonescale_` / `main_` prefix is optional: `first_name`, `job_title`, `company_domain`, `email` and `phone` resolve like their prefixed form, and camelCase keys from enrich payloads (`firstName`, `jobTitle`, ...) are aliased too. A record whose keys match none of the mapped or unicity fields is failed, with the expected field keys in the error.

account_crm_id.description: Optional CRM company id: targets that company directly instead of matching by unicity criteria.

contact_crm_id.description: Optional CRM contact id (e.g. the id returned by POST /crm/search): updates that exact contact instead of matching by unicity criteria.

owner_id.description: Salesforce only. Optional User id (005…) that owns the created or updated Lead or Contact. Without it the CRM keeps its default owner on create and the current owner on update; a mapping row on OwnerId takes precedence.

crm.description: Target CRM. Required only when more than one connected CRM has mapping settings.

settings_type.description: Which team-level settings record to sync with when several exist for the CRM (settings are stored per use-case: api_sync, contact_sourcing, job_changes, ...). When omitted, resolution prefers the dedicated `api_sync` record (configured in the "API Sync" tab of the CRM integration), then falls back to `contact_sourcing`, then the only existing record.

contacts.description: Contacts to create/update (company fields may be embedded on each contact).

webhook_url.description: Called once with the run summary when every record has been processed.

webhook_id.description: Deliver every record to this platform webhook (id from `GET /webhooks`) instead of a CRM. No CRM connection or mapping is required. Mutually exclusive with `crm` / `settings_type`; distinct from `webhook_url` (the completion callback).

idempotency_key.description: Reuse the same key to make client retries return the existing run instead of double-writing.

CrmSearchRequest.description: Flat form: provide `email`, `linkedin_url`, or a name (`first_name`/`last_name`) together with `company_domain` or `company_name`; a name is never searched unconstrained. Records form: `contacts` and/or `companies` (the crm-sync records), answered per record.

contacts.description: Contact records in the crm-sync vocabulary (`main_email`, `lonescale_linkedin_url`, `lonescale_first_name` / `lonescale_last_name`, `lonescale_company_domain` / `lonescale_company_name`; aliases accepted). Each one is searched like the flat form and answered in `contacts[i]`. At most 20 records (contacts + companies) per request.

companies.description: Company records: `lonescale_company_domain`, `lonescale_company_name`, `lonescale_company_linkedin_url` (aliases accepted), or `account_crm_id` to read one by id. Answered in `companies[i]`. Other `lonescale_company_*` keys on the record feed your company unicity criteria.

settings_type.description: Pin the per-use-case settings record (`api_sync`, `contact_sourcing`, …) the search reads its LinkedIn property and unicity criteria from, same values as `POST /trigger/crm-sync`. Only the CRMs carrying that record are searched; 422 when none does.

email.description: Email to look up in the connected CRM(s).

linkedin_url.description: LinkedIn profile URL to look up. HubSpot/Salesforce only.

first_name.description: Used with `last_name` + a company when no email/LinkedIn is available. Matches are fuzzier and reported with a lower `confidence`.

company_domain.description: Constrains a name search to that company. Preferred over `company_name` (more precise).

company_name.description: Fallback company constraint when no domain is known. Yields `confidence: low`.

crm.description: Restrict the search to a single CRM instead of all connected ones.

phone.description: Phone already on the record (mobile first). HubSpot and Salesforce.

profileUrl.description: LinkedIn URL stored on the record

matchedEmail.description: The address that actually matched. HubSpot's contact search also matches secondary addresses, so the record's primary `email` can differ from the one you searched.

matchedOn.description: Which identifier produced the match. `unicity_criteria` means the team's own CRM unicity rules matched (the same rule crm-sync applies).

confidence.description: How much to trust the match. Email / LinkedIn / unicity-criteria hits are `high`; a name constrained by a resolved company is `medium`; a name matched against a free-text company name is `low` (homonym risk) and should be verified before acting.

object.description: Salesforce only: `lead` when the team's mapping writes Leads.

owned_by_you.description: True when the record's owner is the CRM user linked to the API key holder (see `caller_crm_links`). Salesforce ids are compared on their 15-char prefix.

id.description: CRM record id: pass it back as `account_crm_id` to `POST /trigger/crm-sync` to update that company.

domain.description: Website / domain stored on the record

linkedinUrl.description: LinkedIn company page stored on the record

url.description: Link to the record in the CRM. Null on Sellsy.

matchedOn.description: The tier that found it, in search order. `unicity_criteria` is the rule crm-sync applies. A `linkedin` or `name` hit is a record a crm-sync without criteria would not find by domain: pass its id as `account_crm_id`.

confidence.description: `low` for a name hit (homonym risk), `high` for every other tier.

CrmSearchRecordResult.description: The answer for one record of the records form, under the record's position in the request.

error.description: Present when the record carried nothing searchable (`no identifier`): no CRM was queried for it.

CrmLinks.description: The CRM user linked to the API key holder (Settings > Members), per CRM. Records created by a CRM write-back (`sync_to_crm`, Chrome extension) are assigned to that user; `null` means not linked, so created records go to the connection's default owner. Pipedrive/Sellsy have no per-user link.

contacts.description: Records form only: one entry per `contacts[i]` of the request, in order.

companies.description: Records form only: one entry per `companies[i]` of the request, in order.

default_crm.description: The CRM a `crm`-less sync would resolve to (same rules as POST /trigger/crm-sync). Null when ambiguous: ask the user which CRM to act on.

errors.description: Per-CRM lookup failures. Present only when a provider errored. IMPORTANT: an empty `matches` alongside `errors` is NOT a confirmed "no match" — do not treat it as "contact is new".

warnings.description: Lookups a CRM skipped (for example a LinkedIn URL with no LinkedIn property mapped): the other identifiers were searched, so a "no match" is weaker than it looks. Deduplicated across records.

id.description: Run id, used to poll the status endpoint

status.description: Terminal values name the outcome: `finished` = all records synced, `partial` = some failed, `failed` = every record failed. Treat all three as terminal when polling — not only `finished`. The completion webhook carries the same `status` plus `errors_sample`.

errors_sample.description: First few failed records (present only when failed > 0)

warnings.description: Per-CRM lookups that were skipped, not failed: for example a `linkedin_url` was given but no LinkedIn property is mapped in that CRM's settings, so only the other identifiers were searched. Present only when something was skipped. An empty `matches` alongside `warnings` is weaker than a plain "no match": say so to the user before creating a record.

index.description: Position of the record in the submitted payload (contacts first, then companies)

crm_contact_id.description: CRM id of the contact created/updated

crm_company_id.description: CRM id of the company created/updated

id.description: CRM owner id (HubSpot owner id, Salesforce User id).

status.description: `none`: never ranked, call refresh. `pending`: ranking, poll again.

scope.description: The book: `all`, `unassigned`, `owner:<CRM owner id>`, or `unlinked:<user id>` when the caller has no CRM owner.

owner_linked.description: False when the caller's own book was asked and no CRM owner matches their email.

book_size.description: Accounts with a domain in the book.

location.description: City and country from the CRM address; `null` when the CRM has none.

industry.description: The CRM industry; `null` when the CRM has none.

angle.description: Why this person, why now: one line written at list time in the account's language. `null` when it could not be written.
angle.example: Nouveau VP Sales depuis 8 jours : il choisit ses outils maintenant.

crm_id.description: HubSpot company id or Salesforce Account id.

reason.example: Charlotte C. just moved here as Team Lead BDR

person.description: The one to reach first (`people[0]`); `null` when no contact is known.

role.description: Who they are to the purchase, read off the job title; `null` when unclear.

crm_id.description: CRM contact id, when the person is in the CRM.

people.description: The buying committee, the signal's person first: up to 3, one per role when LoneScale or your CRM knows them (more after `find-people`). Older lists carry `[person]`.

last_activity_at.description: Last sales activity on the account; `null` when never contacted.

looks_like_your_wins.description: Industry and size typical of your recent closed-won deals.

former_customer.description: A deal won more than 18 months ago: a win-back. Current customers (a deal won in the last 18 months, or the CRM's customer stage) are never listed.

TodaysAccountPerson.description: A person to reach at a listed account.

role.description: Who they are to the purchase, read off the job title; `null` when unclear.

crm_id.description: CRM contact id, when the person is in the CRM.

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Provide your API key in the x-api-key header.
